object_description: two independent volumes side by side on the southern slope edge, both in timber
geometry_property: concrete plinth under the hall only
design_condition: the two volumes sit on the southern edge of the slope below the castle wall, accessed by two parallel paths at different levels with terracing walls, continuing the development of the landscape space in front of the historic ensemble

positive: The historic courtyard and garden are pleasantly freed from intrusive tree planting
The spatially defined parking is well conceived
The placement and granularity of the two independent volumes on the southern slope edge is promising
It takes up and continues the development of the landscape space in front of the historic ensemble
Dismantling the pool buildings restores the small valley to its original topography
The two new buildings do not tower above the castle wall
Terracing walls structure the access area and are continued as a transition to the neighbouring plots
The direct connection to the neighbouring school complex is integrated into this system
Both buildings follow the same design principle with a uniform timber column grid and varied infill panels
The entrance to the sports hall is in the right place
The two-storey foyer relates well to the hall
Organising the sports hall over three storeys is compact and functional
The entrance to the basic level is attractively located on the intermediate landing of the terraced entrance zone
The mezzanine ground floor allows light to enter the garden level from the south
The four basic level areas are well designed with an attractive inside-outside transition and inserted loggias
Each classroom has a directly accessible and clearly visible outdoor space
The psychomotor room works thanks to the short distance despite its position
Despite splitting into two buildings a relatively good compactness is achieved
The grey energy target is well achieved and the daylight quotient is very good in both buildings
The project has a compact building volume with an average floor area
negative: The parking concept does not integrate the existing spaces, so the unattractive access is additionally burdened
The retained checkroom building by the pool is still a minor nuisance
A height offset between the volumes would have strengthened their independence and integration
The vestibule overcomes a height difference of more than two metres in a confined space
The intermingling of the entrances with the outdoor play areas appears cramped and unattractive
The hall protruding from a concrete plinth is an attempt to conceal its large volume
Making the buildings appear as purely wooden structures contradicts the urban idea and the significance of the new functions
The sports hall entrance is modest in size and therefore not very inviting
The two-storey foyer is confusing and the three-storey staircase has a constricting effect
Organising the hall over three storeys is spatially disadvantageous
The psychomotor room in the hall entrance area is not ideal as it belongs functionally to the basic level
The access situation is complex due to the basic topographical concept
The outdoor spaces for the school are relatively narrow and two metres lower
Walls over one metre require railings that would diminish the open and flowing image shown
The quality of the classroom outdoor spaces is judged to be too variable
Access to the castle garden via the new parking lot is not possible as the address of the school
The positioning of the all-weather pitch in the grass playing field is considered difficult
The large north-facing window areas would have to be significantly optimised for the energy standard
The unprotected wooden facade reduces its service life
Splitting the uses into two buildings and the elaborate landscaping reduce economic efficiency
The project cannot exploit its potential in detail and has too many uncorrectable problem areas
